items.title: More generated cases, better odds of finding a rare bug
items.description: L1's encode/decode bug only showed up on roughly 1 in every 340 randomly generated inputs. Drag the number of generated test cases to see how the chance of hitting that bug at least once climbs — quickly at first, then with diminishing returns, but never guaranteed. 500 cases (L1's default) lands close to the actual run that found it.
items.compute: const perCaseOdds = 1 / 340; const probabilityPercent = Math.round((1 - Math.pow(1 - perCaseOdds, params.numCases)) * 1000) / 10; return { probabilityPercent };

outputs.label: Chance of finding the bug at least once

items.title: How shrinking converges to the minimal counterexample
items.description: L3's raw failure on mergeIntervals started as a messy 4-interval input; shrinking converged it down to the 2-interval minimal counterexample (one interval fully containing another). Drag the number of shrink iterations run to see the failing input shrink toward that floor — most of the reduction happens in the first few iterations, then it flattens out once nothing smaller still fails.
items.compute: const minimalSize = 2; const startSize = 4; const counterexampleSize = Math.round(minimalSize + (startSize - minimalSize) * Math.pow(0.55, params.iterations)); return { counterexampleSize };
